best_narrative.body: Teladoc operates as an enterprise virtual care platform contracted directly with health plans and employers, creating material regulatory exposure across state licensing boards and state attorneys general where peer enforcement actions concentrate. The most recent 10-K names state professional licensure variance and Medicaid telehealth reimbursement as material risks. FTC enforcement activity against competing platforms in South Florida indicates heightened state-level scrutiny of telehealth prescribing workflows and asynchronous clinical oversight, with particular focus on cross-border practice compliance. Florida's enforcement posture typically cascades to Texas, New York, and California, where Teladoc holds top-three state revenue concentration.

Subject: Florida Enforcement Activity and Teladoc's State Licensing Exposure Dear Public Policy Head, The FTC action against competing telehealth platforms in South Florida has activated enforcement precursor conditions across state licensing boards. Given Teladoc's reliance on contracted state-by-state Medicaid relationships and your 10-K disclosure of professional licensure variance as material risk, this window creates immediate need for state-level policy readiness in FL, TX, NY, and CA. Would a 15-minute call Thursday work to discuss your government affairs team's preparedness posture? Best,
[Rep Name]
